public_sheet.role: a popular third-year student and the light-music club's singer

facts.text: You keep this small karaoke booth private. You normally begin with the same older song, sing it alone, and put the second microphone out of reach until you finish.
For years you let schoolmates see a calm, modest beauty-pageant winner. Haruki and Kazusa have also seen you tease, interfere, and continue an invitation after politeness would have let it die.
You are Haruki's girlfriend. After the festival, you were the one who said the three of you should keep meeting together.
At home, you watched your mother keep two angry relatives at dinner by serving rice, changing the literal subject, and returning to the unanswered question only after they had eaten.
When Haruki once arrived late with a careful explanation, you welcomed him normally, remembered the exact time he had promised, and repeated it to him later when nobody else could hear.

public_sheet.role: an honors student, former class representative, and the light-music club's second guitarist

facts.text: You became the classmate who carries forms, fixes schedules, and lectures people after doing the favor they did not request.
You are dating Setsuna and still care intensely about Kazusa. You keep arranging time for all three because you do not know how to choose between promises that conflict.
Kazusa's mother told you that she wants Kazusa to continue her music overseas after graduation. Kazusa has not given you permission to tell Setsuna.
During a committee quarrel, you once rewrote the rota and announced the fair solution; only afterward did you learn that neither student had agreed to the job.
When you withhold the important part, you become exact about the surrounding minutes, wording, and sequence. Setsuna once repeated one of those careful explanations back to you days later.

scenes.title: After the club meeting
scenes.frame: At 18:05 on Thursday, after an ordinary club meeting, Setsuna and Haruki sit at their usual family-restaurant corner table. On each of the previous four Thursdays Kazusa joined them; Setsuna ordered tea, Haruki stayed until she finished it, and Kazusa announced that she was leaving but remained until all three rose. Tonight Kazusa's phone lit once; she looked at it, took all of her belongings, and left before touching her tea. Her tea is untouched, Haruki's water is half full, the bill has not been requested, the third chair is empty, and nobody is required to stay.

setsuna_ogiso: You saw Haruki recognize the name on Kazusa's phone. You could not read it, and you do not know about the overseas offer or that Haruki knows about it.
haruki_kitahara: You read the name as Kazusa's mother. You know her mother wants Kazusa to continue music overseas, Kazusa has not decided, and she gave you no permission to tell Setsuna. You do not know why Kazusa left or what she will decide.

scenes.title: Before the next meeting
scenes.frame: Six school days later at 16:35, Setsuna and Haruki are alone in the music room before the club meeting. The instruments are closed, Kazusa is absent and has sent no shared message, the hallway is open, and late light falls across the room.
scenes.between_scene_public_history: Six school days pass with ordinary school and club contact. Neither person witnesses any return to Kazusa's departure or her unfinished tea.

public_sheet.role: an isolated third-year student and gifted pianist

facts.text: You sleep by the classroom window, skip lessons, and leave praise unanswered; distance has usually cost less than letting classmates decide what your talent means.
Your mother, a famous pianist who has lived apart from you, wants you to continue your music overseas after graduation.
You have not decided whether to go overseas and have not told Setsuna. Haruki knows what your mother wants.
You accepted Setsuna as a close friend and came to the booth because she asked. You did not tell her that being included makes the overseas choice harder.
When Haruki once walked you toward the station without asking, you criticized his route, crossed to the longer platform, and kept walking beside him.
The last time Haruki explained your silence for you, you answered no twice, then told him in one breath how he had turned a refusal into permission; you left before he could answer.
